summary.oneLiner: Strong Q4FY26 revenue growth of 15% YoY and EBITDA margin expansion to 6.7% reflect successful execution of store maturity and category mix shifts, with mobile and large appliances driving demand; what matters is the sustained SSSG of 12.2% and NCR becoming EBITDA-positive, signaling scalable unit economics beyond core South markets.

one-line thesis: Strong Q4FY26 revenue growth of 15% YoY and EBITDA margin expansion to 6.7% reflect successful execution of store maturity and category mix shifts, with mobile and large appliances driving demand; what matters is the sustained SSSG of 12.2% and NCR becoming EBITDA-positive, signaling scalable unit economics beyond core South markets.
financial scorecard: revenue: +15% YoY (INR1,913cr vs INR1,664cr); EBITDA/margin: +20% YoY to INR129cr (6.7% vs 5.6%); PAT (rptd): +49% YoY to INR40cr; PAT (normalized): not disclosed; order book: not disclosed; net debt: reduced working capital needs, CFO of INR299cr for FY26, no explicit debt repayment plan
guidance: revenue growth: implied 7-10% FY27 (FY26 grew 7%); margin: target NCR EBITDA margin of 3-4% by FY28; order inflow: no explicit guidance; capex/commissioning: 12-15 new stores FY27, ~INR3-4cr/store avg, INR50cr+ real estate investment planned for Calcutta entry
segment / subsidiary detail: Large Appliances: 42% mix (down from 47%), driven by GST cuts and festive demand; Washing Machines & Panel TVs: double-digit growth; Refrigerators: stable despite price hikes; Mobile Phones: +28% growth, ASPs up due to premium model focus (avg INR35-40k); Accessories/Audio: higher-margin add-ons improving mix; Cooling: strong Q4 traction, inventory managed ahead of summer
growth verticals / optionality: Entry into Eastern India (Calcutta) with 5-7 stores by Q2/Q3 FY27; potential future expansion into UP, Goa, Dehradun; no franchise model yet but under internal review
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin: 6.7% (Q4), 6.1% (FY26); mature stores: 7.3%, new stores: 3.1%; margin improvement driven by higher-margin accessories, reduced distributor reliance (only INR50cr/year), and improved SKU-level pricing discipline; GST reduction enabled volume-driven margin expansion
capex / expansion: INR3-4cr per store avg; 12-15 new stores planned FY27; Calcutta entry requires INR50-100cr real estate investment over 12-14 months; all stores 6k-12k sq ft, avg 8k-10k sq ft
capital allocation: CFO of INR299cr in FY26 deployed to reduce working capital; no debt repayment planned beyond organic loan amortization; reinvestment prioritized into store expansion and inventory efficiency; no dividends or buybacks mentioned
risks & watch-items: Competition intensifying in NCR (Croma, Reliance); price hikes in RAC and mobiles passed to customers, risking volume if demand elasticity kicks in; new geography entry (Calcutta) execution risk; dependency on monsoon and summer demand cycles
management quality / tone: Confident, disciplined, and long-term oriented; CEO emphasizes control over customer experience, rejects franchise model for quality reasons; avoids giving FY27 guidance due to seasonal uncertainty; highlights operational rigor and margin discipline
non-obvious takeaways: Despite 140 new stores (<4 yrs), SSSG of 12.2% in Q4 implies strong underlying demand, not just store expansion; mobile ASPs rising despite industry-wide deflation due to premium SKU focus; NCR profitability achieved without franchise capital efficiency — a testament to operational excellence

themes.title: Quick-commerce, omnichannel & retail expansion
themes.need: Quick-commerce and value retail are the structural growth engine, and Q1FY27 rewrote the unit-economics model. ETERNAL raised Blinkit's steady-state margin from a 5-6% range to ~6% and set a first-ever 4% GAAP EBIT margin target (after ESOP and depreciation) while capex per store went from INR 1cr to INR 2.5cr (+150%) with NOV/store/day up only 60% and net working capital improving 18 to 14 days - so margin can now drift DOWN while ROCE improves. Growth also decoupled from spend: Blinkit orders +21% QoQ with MTUs above 30mn achieved on LOWER marketing spend and fewer store adds, and management called Q1 the peak of competitive intensity to date. VMM did INR 3,727cr (+18.7%) on 10% SSSG with gross margin up to 28.7% driven by lower promotional spend rather than price hikes, validated a small-format store at the same revenue/sq ft and 'pretty much the same' ROCE as large format (a ~3,000-store national opportunity), and found 20% of its quick-commerce customers had never shopped a Vishal store. SHOPERSTOP swung PAT positive (+INR 5cr vs -INR 4cr) and raised FY27 LFL guidance from 5% to ~6%; ARVINDFASN lifted gross margin 90bps to 56.7% on full-price sell-through with direct channels now 62% of sales; MEESHO cut cost per delivered order ~INR 1 QoQ despite the May fuel hike. DMART/V2RETAIL/PATELRMART on value retail; TRENT-tier branded retail via ABFRL/METROBRAND/BATAINDIA/REDTAPE.
themes.driver: Blinkit dark-store rollout at the new INR 2.5cr/store capex against the 4% GAAP EBIT target; VMM small-format expansion; festive/quick-commerce GMV. Watch ARVINDFASN's SS27 sourcing lock (next 45-60 days) - if war-inflated input costs hold, apparel pricing corrects.

themes.title: Consumer durables, cooling & electricals
themes.need: Rising incomes, electrification and a record cooling season drive consumer-electricals and appliances - HAVELLS/VOLTAS/BLUESTARCO/SYMPHONY/ORIENTELEC on cooling & electricals; TTKPRESTIG/STOVEKRAFT/BAJAJELEC/EUREKAFORB on kitchen/home; CROMPTON-tier fans & pumps; premiumization + GST 2.0 + summer demand expand the organized share. Q1FY27's small-cap read: SONAMLTD grew revenue 75.6% YoY to INR 66.57cr on a cheap raw-material inventory position taken 6-7 months in advance while selling prices rose - management explicitly called the 75% print non-repeatable and guided FY27 to 25-30% with a Q2 floor of INR 40-50cr - and is pivoting from volume to INR 5,000-15,000 value clocks with capacity utilisation still only 60-70%.
themes.driver: Summer cooling demand; GST 2.0 price cuts; festive restocking; commodity-cost tailwind on margins; premiumization/ASP mix shift.
